definition: Breadth-first search explores a graph in layers, visiting every neighbor of the current layer before going deeper. It uses a queue so the oldest discovered vertex is expanded next. On an unweighted graph, the first time it reaches a vertex is along a shortest path by number of edges.
details: A seen set is required, or a cycle makes the search run forever.
On a tree there is no cycle, but the seen set still avoids nothing extra if each node has one parent.

complexity.time: O(V + E) with an adjacency list.
complexity.space: O(V) for the queue and the seen set.

examples: The fewest hops between two people in a social graph
Spreading a flood fill one ring at a time
